[3/3] Plan: strict --since grammar, WYSIWYG min-score filter, cumulative git timeout budget

impact_assessment.why: Three recorded verification gaps: git's approxidate silently accepts garbage --since (banana/0/1.unit.ago parse to now-like dates, exit 0 with a truncated or empty report); --min-score compares the 4-decimal internal score while the table shows 3 decimals, so a 0.300-displayed row can be filtered out at --min-score 0.3; git log --numstat on a huge repo can exceed the fixed 60s per-call timeout with no cumulative budget
impact_assessment.benefits: WYSIWYG CLI: every accepted input and filtered row matches what the user sees; malformed relative dates fail at argparse (exit 2) before any git call; long numstat walks get an explicit bounded budget instead of a thin 60s window
impact_assessment.risks: contract: --since now rejects approxidate strings outside the documented grammar (deliberate, message lists accepted forms); dependency: none (stdlib regexes); concurrency: budget state is module-level but driftwood is single-threaded per invocation; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: grammar helper is pure regex, unit-tested subtest-per-form; budget ships as a git_session() context manager so library users and the 2-arg Runner fakes keep the old contract; failing-first tests per gap

[3/3] Plan: --format csv, --group-by dir, --all zero-churn inclusion

impact_assessment.why: Recorded improvement backlog from the verification passes: output is limited to table/json, grouping by directory requires external scripting, and files with no commit history are invisible in the report even though their complexity makes them risk material
impact_assessment.benefits: CSV gives scriptable spreadsheet-compatible output; dir grouping answers 'which area churns' directly; --all surfaces new uncommitted files whose complexity is invisible today
impact_assessment.risks: contract: --format gains a choice and two new flags, all additive; CSV score column follows the 3-decimal display precision (WYSIWYG) while JSON keeps stored precision; --all can produce large tables (bounded by --top); grouping semantics: top-level files group as '.', aggregation is additive sums before ranking
impact_assessment.mitigation: each feature is one milestone with failing-first tests; reuse rank_hotspots for grouped scoring so tie-breaking and drop rules stay single-sourced; ls-files --exclude-standard respects .gitignore; README updated same commit per milestone
